scope: URL-to-Flow canonical classification, source-access, rights, review and projection contract
claimBoundary: This catalog and its automated agreement tests are contract QA, not observed-user validation or legal advice.
preservedCanonicalDecisions: SourceRow is the minimum provenance unit.
Item is the minimum independently stateful execution and projection unit.
Step groups Items and does not own completion state.
Flow has one user job and one primary source.
Calendar, checklist, todo, sheet and memo are projections, not canonical storage units.
Source evidence, published content, user overlay, run state and internal review remain separately owned.
classificationOrder: Verify that actual source rows are available.
Write the immediate user job without category words.
Choose primaryLifeArea by the immediate real-world outcome.
Choose sourceShape from the anatomy of the available source rows.
Choose primaryExecutionPattern from the state transition the user repeats or completes.
Choose primaryArtifact as the one artifact the user must retain to finish the job.
Record audience and applicability separately from user-need and friction signals.
Record discovery, row access and acquisition independently.
Record rights basis, allowed use and territory independently.
Evaluate source, freshness, locale, safety, privacy, rights and promotion in parallel.

hierarchy.sourceRow: Smallest locatable fact, row, date, instruction, criterion or resource in a source snapshot.
hierarchy.item: Smallest source-backed unit that can independently be completed, decided, recorded, consumed or held.
hierarchy.step: Ordered semantic group of Items; never the authoritative owner of completion or schedule.
hierarchy.flow: One user job with one primary source, one primary execution pattern and one primary artifact.
hierarchy.bundle: A Flow Map or collection of related Flows; grouping only.

fieldSemantics.primaryLifeArea: Exactly one shelf chosen by the immediate user outcome, not by publisher, source format or every topic mentioned.
fieldSemantics.secondaryLifeAreas: Zero to two materially relevant contexts that change discovery or applicability but do not own the immediate outcome.
fieldSemantics.topicTags: Search and retrieval vocabulary. Tags never substitute for a life area or gate.
fieldSemantics.sourceShape: The dominant anatomy of the rows actually acquired from the source snapshot.
fieldSemantics.secondarySourceShapes: Additional row anatomy only when the same source genuinely contains both; never used to avoid choosing a dominant shape.
fieldSemantics.primaryExecutionPattern: The state transition the user must complete or repeat to achieve the Flow job.
fieldSemantics.secondaryExecutionPatterns: A supporting interaction that is useful but not sufficient to complete the user job.
fieldSemantics.primaryArtifact: The one retained artifact without which the user cannot finish or resume the job.
fieldSemantics.secondaryArtifacts: Loss-aware projections that add convenience; must not repeat primaryArtifact.
fieldSemantics.userNeedSignals: What job support the user needs.
fieldSemantics.frictionSignals: What currently makes that job inconvenient. Former targetConditions are mapped to one of these two lists, never copied as free text.
fieldSemantics.sourceFormatDetail: Descriptive metadata such as MIME, page count or transcript availability. It is not an enum extension point.
fieldSemantics.backendStorable: Whether the metadata, snapshot references and currently supported rows can be stored without asserting public rights.
fieldSemantics.personalTransformAllowed: Product policy for a reviewed private copy; independent of public release and not a legal conclusion.
fieldSemantics.publicReleaseAllowed: Derived publication gate; never inferred only from public access.

home_living.definition: Maintaining, moving into, organizing or operating a home or owned household object.
home_living.chooseWhen: The immediate outcome is a usable home, room, appliance or household system.
home_living.excludeWhen: The immediate outcome is travel, a purchase decision, family caregiving or meal preparation.
home_living.tieBreaker: Choose the object whose state changes; a contract choice is money_admin_purchase, later move execution is home_living.
home_living.secondaryRule: Use as secondary for a purchase or family Flow only when home constraints change applicability.
home_living.goodExample: 이사 D-30 — the home transition is the outcome.
home_living.badExample: 전세계약 후보 비교 — the decision, not household operation, is the outcome.

family_parenting.definition: Care, coordination, development or shared execution centered on a child, dependent or family role.
family_parenting.chooseWhen: The job would materially change without the caregiver/dependent relationship.
family_parenting.excludeWhen: Family members are merely companions in a trip, meal or event whose primary outcome belongs elsewhere.
family_parenting.tieBreaker: Ask whether success is better caregiving/development or completion of the trip, study or health appointment.
family_parenting.secondaryRule: Family travel is travel_outings primary and family_parenting secondary unless caregiving itself is the job.
family_parenting.goodExample: 그림책 질문 루틴 — parent-child interaction is the outcome.
family_parenting.badExample: 가족여행 D-7 — the trip preparation is the outcome.

study_reading.definition: Learning, reading, practice or curriculum completion whose immediate output is competence or progress.
study_reading.chooseWhen: The user is consuming lessons, chapters or practice rows to learn.
study_reading.excludeWhen: The learning is only a means to ship a professional deliverable or change employment state.
study_reading.tieBreaker: A developer course is study_reading when lesson progress is the job; work_career when a portfolio, interview or work deliverable is the terminal output.
study_reading.secondaryRule: Add work_career for role-specific upskilling with a clear professional application.
study_reading.badExample: 개발 포트폴리오 4주 — shipping the portfolio is the outcome.

money_admin_purchase.definition: Eligibility, documents, public administration, money, contracts, purchase comparison or formal decision.
money_admin_purchase.chooseWhen: The terminal state is submitted, eligible, contracted, selected, paid or officially confirmed.
money_admin_purchase.excludeWhen: The administrative act only anchors a larger travel, home or health execution and is not the Flow job.
money_admin_purchase.tieBreaker: Choose this when the durable output is a decision, document or official status.
money_admin_purchase.secondaryRule: Use as secondary when a travel or life event includes meaningful official paperwork.
money_admin_purchase.badExample: 이사 당일 체크 — the home transition owns the job.

health_fitness.definition: Exercise, health service logistics, prevention or personal physical routine.
health_fitness.chooseWhen: The immediate outcome is a session, health appointment or safe physical practice.
health_fitness.excludeWhen: The source is occupational safety for a team or food storage guidance whose primary job is elsewhere.
health_fitness.tieBreaker: Choose the context where action happens: occupational heat safety is work_career primary, health_fitness secondary.
health_fitness.secondaryRule: Use for safety/health consequences that materially alter another job.
health_fitness.badExample: 농작업 온열질환 팀 점검 — workplace execution is primary.

travel_outings.definition: Planning, preparing, selecting or executing a trip, outing or visit experience.
travel_outings.chooseWhen: The destination, departure or outing is the immediate outcome.
travel_outings.excludeWhen: The activity is primarily a child-development routine or formal document issuance.
travel_outings.tieBreaker: Family composition is audience context; choose travel when the artifact still makes sense as a trip plan.
travel_outings.secondaryRule: Add family_parenting when child/caregiver constraints affect the rows.
travel_outings.badExample: 여권 재발급 서류 — official administration is the job.

meals_grocery.definition: Choosing, preparing, cooking, storing or rotating food and groceries.
meals_grocery.chooseWhen: The terminal output is a meal, menu, grocery state or food-storage action.
meals_grocery.excludeWhen: The core job is clinical nutrition treatment or family-development tracking.
meals_grocery.tieBreaker: Choose meals_grocery for food execution; add health/family only as a secondary applicability context.
meals_grocery.secondaryRule: Sensitive dietary context belongs in safety/applicability, not a forced primary category change.
meals_grocery.badExample: 체중 감량 치료 계획 — health_fitness owns the outcome.

work_career.definition: Professional delivery, employment transition, workplace operation or creator/operator production.
work_career.chooseWhen: The terminal result is shipped work, a role change, a workplace process or a professional portfolio.
work_career.excludeWhen: The user is only studying a course without a named professional deliverable.
work_career.tieBreaker: Deliverable/status beats subject matter: course progress is study; portfolio shipment is work.
work_career.secondaryRule: Add study_reading when structured learning rows are a substantial subjob.
work_career.badExample: MDN 학습 모듈 진도 — learning progress is the job.

hobby_pet.definition: Leisure making, creative practice, personal collections, plants or pet care outside a dominant family/work/health job.
hobby_pet.chooseWhen: The activity or owned living object is primarily recreational or pet/plant care.
hobby_pet.excludeWhen: The same activity is a professional deliverable, family-development job or home maintenance job.
hobby_pet.tieBreaker: Choose by who/what owns the outcome: child play is family; professional craft is work; personal craft is hobby.
hobby_pet.secondaryRule: Use as secondary for a family activity with a genuine craft or pet-care subjob.
hobby_pet.badExample: 아이와 공룡 미술 놀이 — family interaction is primary.

single_action.definition: One source-backed action or one follow-along resource with no independently stateful subrows.
single_action.chooseWhen: Splitting the source would invent checks or duplicate the resource.
single_action.excludeWhen: The source names several independently checkable rows.
single_action.tieBreaker: If one action can be completed without preserving an internal order, use single_action.
single_action.primarySecondaryRule: Primary when one action carries the job; narrative detail stays Memo.
single_action.goodExample: 오늘 원본 운동 영상 한 번 따라하기.
single_action.badExample: A five-step application guide collapsed to one action.

checklist_rows.definition: Named rows that can be independently checked in any or grouped order.
checklist_rows.chooseWhen: Row-level omission matters more than strict sequence.
checklist_rows.excludeWhen: Changing order breaks the task or rows are table records rather than checks.
checklist_rows.tieBreaker: If order can change without changing meaning, prefer checklist_rows.
checklist_rows.primarySecondaryRule: Use secondary procedure_rows only when one subset has a required order.
checklist_rows.badExample: eSIM 활성화 순서를 unordered checks로 분류.

date_offsets.definition: Rows anchored to D-day, start date, birth date or another source-defined offset.
date_offsets.chooseWhen: The source supplies offsets that determine when rows occur.
date_offsets.excludeWhen: It supplies only one due window or the user invents the dates.
date_offsets.tieBreaker: Two or more meaningful offsets beat generic table anatomy.
date_offsets.primarySecondaryRule: Table may be secondary if offsets are represented as rows and columns.
date_offsets.badExample: One official renewal period labeled date_offsets.

date_window.definition: One or more official start/end or due-by windows without a source-defined preparation sequence.
date_window.chooseWhen: The source fact is eligibility or action inside a time window.
date_window.excludeWhen: The source defines multiple anchor-relative preparation rows.
date_window.tieBreaker: Use date_window when preserving both boundaries is more important than ordering actions.
date_window.primarySecondaryRule: May pair with checklist_rows for required documents.

recurrence_rule.definition: A source-defined cadence, interval or repeat condition that is itself the executable evidence.
recurrence_rule.chooseWhen: The source supplies when to repeat but no independently stateful row set.
recurrence_rule.excludeWhen: The cadence is invented by the user/adapter or distinct resources define each occurrence.
recurrence_rule.tieBreaker: If removing the cadence destroys the source-specific value, use recurrence_rule; otherwise keep it as metadata on another shape.
recurrence_rule.primarySecondaryRule: single_action is commonly secondary because one action is repeated.
recurrence_rule.badExample: A user arbitrarily schedules an article every Monday.

procedure_rows.definition: Source steps whose order or dependency is required to complete the task.
procedure_rows.chooseWhen: Skipping or reordering a row can cause failure.
procedure_rows.excludeWhen: Rows are independent checks, alternatives or comparison criteria.
procedure_rows.tieBreaker: Required dependency, not numbered typography, determines procedure_rows.
procedure_rows.primarySecondaryRule: Checklist rows may be secondary for prerequisites or final verification.
procedure_rows.badExample: Ten contract criteria numbered for readability.

table_rows.definition: Repeated records with stable columns whose values must be compared, filtered or updated.
table_rows.chooseWhen: Column semantics are essential to the job.
table_rows.excludeWhen: The source merely lays out prose in a visual table.
table_rows.tieBreaker: If removing columns destroys meaning, choose table_rows.
table_rows.primarySecondaryRule: Lesson rows override when rows are explicitly instructional units and progress is the job.

lesson_rows.definition: Named lessons, chapters, modules, assignments or tests supplied by a curriculum.
lesson_rows.chooseWhen: Rows identify learning units rather than generic resources.
lesson_rows.excludeWhen: The source is an unstructured channel or reading list.
lesson_rows.tieBreaker: A source-defined learning dependency or completion unit beats collection format.
lesson_rows.primarySecondaryRule: Table rows may be secondary when the curriculum includes stable status columns.
lesson_rows.badExample: A creator video channel without imported lesson order.

resource_collection.definition: Distinct articles, videos, books, files or places that can be queued or selected.
resource_collection.chooseWhen: Each row is primarily a resource identity and link.
resource_collection.excludeWhen: Rows are curriculum units with source-defined completion dependencies.
resource_collection.tieBreaker: If user choice/order can vary and the link is the durable value, use resource_collection.
resource_collection.primarySecondaryRule: Lesson rows may be secondary only if the collection contains a documented sequence.
resource_collection.badExample: A course syllabus with required module order.

decision_criteria.definition: Source-backed criteria or option rows whose values lead to select, hold, reject or escalate.
decision_criteria.chooseWhen: Rows must preserve decision meaning rather than binary completion alone.
decision_criteria.excludeWhen: The rows are mandatory checks before one inevitable action.
decision_criteria.tieBreaker: Multiple valid terminal states or option comparison makes decision_criteria primary.
decision_criteria.primarySecondaryRule: table_rows can be secondary when options and criterion values form a matrix.
decision_criteria.goodExample: 리모델링 계약 조건별 진행/보류 판단 기준.
decision_criteria.badExample: Required passport documents with no choice.

narrative_guidance.definition: Explanatory prose containing principles, criteria or advice rather than stable executable rows.
narrative_guidance.chooseWhen: The source can support one application/decision Item plus Memo but not many source rows.
narrative_guidance.excludeWhen: No concrete action, decision or template can be grounded; then conversion is hold.
narrative_guidance.tieBreaker: Narrative describes why/how; single_action describes what to do.
narrative_guidance.primarySecondaryRule: Often secondary to a single action; never split prose into fake Items.
narrative_guidance.goodExample: 한 끼에 적용할 식사 기준 설명.
narrative_guidance.badExample: Turning every paragraph into a checklist Item.

template_fields.definition: A source-defined reusable form, prompt set or structured blank whose fields are the source rows.
template_fields.chooseWhen: The user fills stable fields to create a decision, record or deliverable.
template_fields.excludeWhen: Fields are invented by FlowMe or access to the template is unavailable.
template_fields.tieBreaker: If rows describe what to enter rather than what to execute, use template_fields.
template_fields.primarySecondaryRule: Use table_rows secondary when repeated instances become rows.
template_fields.goodExample: Source-provided science fair project planner fields.
template_fields.badExample: Inferring template fields from a sales page.

date_preparation.definition: Anchor-relative or fixed-date actions whose timing is the main coordination mechanism.
date_preparation.chooseWhen: The user asks what to do when before/after an event.
date_preparation.excludeWhen: Dates are optional milestones on a state-gated project.
date_preparation.tieBreaker: Calendar time advances the Flow even if outputs are incomplete; choose date_preparation.
date_preparation.primarySecondaryRule: phase_lifecycle may be secondary only when named deliverables also gate progress.
date_preparation.badExample: 4주 포트폴리오 whose artifacts gate the next phase.

ordered_procedure.definition: Complete source-backed actions in a dependency-preserving order.
ordered_procedure.chooseWhen: The user succeeds by following the sequence.
ordered_procedure.excludeWhen: The user succeeds by comparing options and choosing one.
ordered_procedure.tieBreaker: If the terminal state is a selected/held option, compare_decide wins; if it is a completed process, ordered_procedure wins.
ordered_procedure.primarySecondaryRule: compare_decide may be secondary for one fork inside a larger procedure.

repeating_routine.definition: Repeat the same action or small stable set on a cadence, with occurrence state.
repeating_routine.chooseWhen: Cadence and next occurrence are the durable state.
repeating_routine.excludeWhen: Each occurrence consumes a distinct resource or advances a finite curriculum.
repeating_routine.tieBreaker: Same action repeats = routine; distinct resources advance = queue; stable completion rows = progress.
repeating_routine.primarySecondaryRule: resource_queue can be secondary when rotating books/videos inside a reading routine.
repeating_routine.badExample: Twelve distinct course videos labeled routine only because they are weekly.

progress_tracking.definition: Advance through stable rows while retaining current position, status or values.
progress_tracking.chooseWhen: The core question is where am I and what is next.
progress_tracking.excludeWhen: Rows are only links to consume in flexible order or phases produce different deliverables.
progress_tracking.tieBreaker: Stable homogeneous rows and status columns = progress; heterogeneous deliverables = lifecycle.
progress_tracking.primarySecondaryRule: resource_queue may be secondary when each progress row links to a resource.

resource_queue.definition: Select and consume distinct resources while keeping the next resource visible.
resource_queue.chooseWhen: Resource identity and ordering/selection are the durable state.
resource_queue.excludeWhen: The source defines homogeneous instructional progress or one repeated action.
resource_queue.tieBreaker: Flexible distinct resources = queue; fixed lesson status = progress; same action = routine.
resource_queue.primarySecondaryRule: progress may be secondary when consumed/not-started status is useful.
resource_queue.goodExample: LibriVox chapter/audio queue selected by the user.
resource_queue.badExample: One picture book reread every weekend.

compare_decide.definition: Evaluate options or criteria and end with select, hold, reject or escalate.
compare_decide.chooseWhen: The decision state is the terminal output.
compare_decide.excludeWhen: Criteria are merely prechecks before one inevitable procedure.
compare_decide.tieBreaker: If multiple valid outcomes remain after checks, compare_decide; otherwise procedure.
compare_decide.primarySecondaryRule: ordered_procedure may follow as a secondary pattern after selection.
compare_decide.goodExample: 리모델링 계약 조건 비교 후 보류/진행 결정.
compare_decide.badExample: Online application steps with no option choice.

phase_lifecycle.definition: Advance through heterogeneous phases where each phase produces a prerequisite result for the next.
phase_lifecycle.chooseWhen: Named outputs and state gates, not dates alone, define progress.
phase_lifecycle.excludeWhen: Rows are homogeneous lessons or simple anchor offsets.
phase_lifecycle.tieBreaker: Different phase outputs/dependencies = lifecycle; same row schema = progress; time-only = date preparation.
phase_lifecycle.primarySecondaryRule: date_preparation may be secondary when deadlines schedule the lifecycle.
phase_lifecycle.badExample: A weekly video playlist with identical completion rows.

calendar.definition: Dated or recurring events whose timing must travel outside FlowMe.
calendar.chooseWhen: Missing the date/cadence breaks the job.
calendar.excludeWhen: Dates are optional reminders added to an otherwise row- or decision-first job.
calendar.tieBreaker: Ask what the user must open on the day of action; if the calendar event is sufficient, calendar is primary.
calendar.primarySecondaryRule: Checklist can be secondary inside event notes; do not call the pair hybrid.
calendar.badExample: A comparison table with optional review date.

checklist.definition: A bounded set of independent checks whose omission state matters during one job.
checklist.chooseWhen: The user needs to see what remains unchecked.
checklist.excludeWhen: The rows need stable comparison/progress columns or are a future resource queue.
checklist.tieBreaker: Bounded verification set = checklist; open next-action queue = todo; columns/status history = sheet.
checklist.primarySecondaryRule: Calendar may be secondary if the checklist has one optional due date.
checklist.badExample: Course lesson progress requiring status and notes.

todo.definition: An open queue of next actions or resources that may be reordered or deferred.
todo.chooseWhen: The durable value is the next actionable queue, not verifying a fixed set.
todo.excludeWhen: The set is bounded and omission-sensitive or needs columns.
todo.tieBreaker: If new rows can be appended naturally and order may change, prefer todo.
todo.primarySecondaryRule: Sheet may be secondary for optional metadata on a large queue.

sheet.definition: Stable rows and columns used to compare, track, filter or record values.
sheet.chooseWhen: Removing columns loses the primary user state.
sheet.excludeWhen: A binary bounded checklist or pure memo is sufficient.
sheet.tieBreaker: If the user returns to change status/value per row, sheet wins.
sheet.primarySecondaryRule: Calendar is secondary for milestones; checklist is secondary for a field visit view.
sheet.badExample: A six-item packing list with no meaningful columns.

memo.definition: Context, criteria, selected rationale, source boundary or a reusable note is the durable output.
memo.chooseWhen: There is one real application/decision and retaining context matters more than row state.
memo.excludeWhen: Independent checks, dates or rows are required to execute.
memo.tieBreaker: If a static note still completes the job, memo; otherwise choose the stateful artifact.
memo.primarySecondaryRule: Memo is commonly secondary but primary only when context itself is the retained result.
memo.goodExample: 선택 이유와 다음 행동을 남기는 결정 메모.
memo.badExample: Twelve dated preparation actions flattened to prose.

providerTypes.definition: The controlled top-level identity of the party responsible for the source, not its host or format.
providerTypes.chooseWhen: Choose from verified publisher ownership or provider identity.
providerTypes.excludeWhen: Do not encode a brand name, domain, content format or access mode here.
providerTypes.tieBreaker: Prefer the party accountable for the content; keep the specific organization in source metadata.
providerTypes.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one provider type; platform roles may be multiple.
providerTypes.goodExample: A ministry guide hosted on its portal is government_public.

valueDefinitions.government_public: A national or local government body publishing official public information.
valueDefinitions.public_institution: A public agency or institution with official operational authority.
valueDefinitions.brand_official: A commercial brand publishing its own product, service or workflow material.
valueDefinitions.creator: An identifiable individual or creator team publishing original material.
valueDefinitions.editorial_media: A publisher whose primary role is edited news, magazine or reference content.
valueDefinitions.community_platform: A platform whose source value comes mainly from member contributions.
valueDefinitions.marketplace: A platform centered on listing or selling products, services or digital goods.
valueDefinitions.education_provider: A school, academy or course provider responsible for instruction.
valueDefinitions.open_knowledge: An open knowledge or open-source project maintaining reusable public material.
valueDefinitions.aggregator: A service that discovers or indexes material mainly owned elsewhere.
valueDefinitions.user_owned: A private file or record the user owns or is authorized to provide.

platformRoles.definition: The roles a platform plays in the source-to-execution journey.
platformRoles.excludeWhen: Do not infer entitlement, execution or distribution from hosting alone.
platformRoles.tieBreaker: Use multiple roles when they are simultaneously evidenced; there is no forced primary role.
platformRoles.primarySecondaryRule: Multi-select; at least one role is required.
platformRoles.goodExample: Todoist can discover, host, execute and enforce entitlement.

valueDefinitions.discover: Users can find or preview the content there.
valueDefinitions.host: The platform serves the authoritative or provider-controlled source.
valueDefinitions.distribute: The platform syndicates or delivers content to audiences.
valueDefinitions.execute: Users can carry out or track the Flow on the platform.
valueDefinitions.export_destination: The platform can receive a Flow projection.
valueDefinitions.entitlement: The platform controls account, purchase or eligibility access.
valueDefinitions.community_signal: The platform exposes reactions, saves, ratings or other audience signals.

discoveryAccess.definition: Whether a person can reach the discovery or landing surface.
discoveryAccess.chooseWhen: Classify the public-facing discovery surface separately from execution rows.
discoveryAccess.excludeWhen: Do not downgrade a public landing page merely because full rows require login.
discoveryAccess.tieBreaker: Judge the landing surface only; record row restrictions in rowAccess.
discoveryAccess.goodExample: Public template page plus OAuth rows = public discovery, partial row access.
discoveryAccess.badExample: account_required solely because copying the template requires login.

valueDefinitions.public: The discovery surface is reachable without an account.
valueDefinitions.account_required: An account is required even to reach the discovery surface.
valueDefinitions.paywalled: Payment is required to reach the meaningful discovery surface.
valueDefinitions.robots_limited: Human access may exist but automated acquisition is explicitly limited.
valueDefinitions.unavailable: The discovery surface cannot currently be reached.
valueDefinitions.unknown: The access state has not been verified.

rowAccess.definition: How much of the source rows needed for the intended Flow is actually obtainable.
rowAccess.chooseWhen: Compare acquired rows with the intended user job.
rowAccess.excludeWhen: Do not treat title, summary or count as full rows.
rowAccess.tieBreaker: Access describes obtainability; sourceRowStatus describes the current captured packet.
rowAccess.goodExample: Four public phase names but hidden tasks = partial.
rowAccess.badExample: full because the landing page is public.

valueDefinitions.full: All rows needed for the bounded Flow are obtainable.
valueDefinitions.partial: Some needed rows are obtainable and some are not.
valueDefinitions.metadata_only: Only descriptive metadata, counts or labels are obtainable.
valueDefinitions.unavailable: Required rows cannot currently be obtained.
valueDefinitions.unknown: Row access has not been verified.

acquisitionMethods.definition: Approved technical or user-mediated methods that can acquire source evidence.
acquisitionMethods.chooseWhen: Record only methods supported by the source and permission boundary.
acquisitionMethods.excludeWhen: Do not list a method merely because it is technically possible.
acquisitionMethods.tieBreaker: Prefer the most authoritative structured method; keep multiple methods when complementary.
acquisitionMethods.primarySecondaryRule: Multi-select; empty is valid when acquisition is unknown or unavailable.
acquisitionMethods.goodExample: Public API plus creator delivery recorded together.

valueDefinitions.pdf_fetch: Acquire rows from a PDF document.
valueDefinitions.rss_fetch: Acquire entries from an RSS or Atom feed.
valueDefinitions.public_api: Acquire from a public documented API.
valueDefinitions.manual_copy: Acquire a bounded excerpt through explicit manual copy.
valueDefinitions.transcript_import: Acquire a transcript supplied or permitted for import.
valueDefinitions.table_import: Acquire structured rows from CSV, XLSX or another table.
valueDefinitions.creator_delivery: Acquire a source package directly from the provider.

sourceFormatCategories.definition: A controlled coarse format family; MIME type and provider-specific details stay in metadata.
sourceFormatCategories.chooseWhen: Choose the dominant acquired source container.
sourceFormatCategories.excludeWhen: Do not create provider- or title-specific format enum values.
sourceFormatCategories.tieBreaker: Format describes the container; sourceShape describes row anatomy after extraction.
sourceFormatCategories.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one coarse format; details are free metadata.
sourceFormatCategories.goodExample: video with lesson_rows after transcript extraction.

valueDefinitions.checklist: A source presented as checks or tick rows.
valueDefinitions.table: A source presented as stable rows and columns.
valueDefinitions.document: PDF, DOCX or similar document container.
valueDefinitions.collection: A collection or index of resources.
valueDefinitions.api_feed: A structured API or feed response.
valueDefinitions.interactive_page: A page whose meaningful result depends on interaction.

audienceRoles.definition: Evidenced user roles affected by applicability or execution.
audienceRoles.chooseWhen: Record roles named or materially implied by the bounded user job.
audienceRoles.excludeWhen: Do not infer demographic identity from topic alone.
audienceRoles.tieBreaker: Roles describe people; collaboration describes how they coordinate.
audienceRoles.primarySecondaryRule: Multi-select with no semantic primary; at least one role.
audienceRoles.goodExample: A family trip may include traveler and caregiver.

valueDefinitions.individual: A general person acting for themselves.
valueDefinitions.professional: A person acting in a work role.
valueDefinitions.creator_operator: A creator or operator running a content/service workflow.
valueDefinitions.team_member: A participant in shared team execution.
valueDefinitions.buyer: A person comparing, contracting or purchasing.
valueDefinitions.traveler: A person planning or taking an outing or trip.

ageBands.definition: Age applicability explicitly supported by source or policy.
ageBands.excludeWhen: Do not infer age from tone or imagery.
ageBands.tieBreaker: Use not_specified when the source does not define an age boundary.
ageBands.primarySecondaryRule: Multi-select; all_ages must not be combined with narrower bands.
ageBands.goodExample: teen for a source explicitly written for secondary students.
ageBands.badExample: adult because the page has complex prose.

skillLevels.definition: Required prior skill for successful execution.
skillLevels.chooseWhen: Use source prerequisites or explicit teaching level.
skillLevels.excludeWhen: Do not infer from content length alone.
skillLevels.tieBreaker: Use mixed for a real range and not_applicable when skill is irrelevant.
skillLevels.goodExample: beginner for a no-prerequisite introductory course.
skillLevels.badExample: advanced because it has many lessons.

valueDefinitions.not_applicable: Skill level does not govern use.

applicability.definition: How directly the content applies in the target locale.
applicability.chooseWhen: Compare rules, language, services and cultural assumptions with target locale.
applicability.excludeWhen: Do not equate translation with legal or service applicability.
applicability.tieBreaker: Applicability is the content property; localeReview is the review state.
applicability.goodExample: US public-domain audiobook marked local_adaptation_required for Korean rights review.
applicability.badExample: global_general merely because the page is in English.

valueDefinitions.local_direct: Directly usable in the target locale.
valueDefinitions.global_general: General guidance not tied to one locale.

accountOrEntitlement.definition: The minimum account, ownership, payment or eligibility condition for required rows or execution.
accountOrEntitlement.excludeWhen: Do not infer entitlement from public discovery.
accountOrEntitlement.tieBreaker: Choose the condition blocking required rows or use, not optional conveniences.
accountOrEntitlement.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one dominant requirement; details stay in prerequisites.
accountOrEntitlement.goodExample: free_account for a template copy requiring login.
accountOrEntitlement.badExample: none because the landing page is public.

valueDefinitions.none: No account or entitlement is required.
valueDefinitions.paid_subscription: An active paid subscription is required.
valueDefinitions.owned_product: Ownership of a product or service is required.
valueDefinitions.source_file_required: The user must supply the source file.

collaborationContext.definition: The coordination model needed to execute the Flow.
collaborationContext.chooseWhen: Choose from ownership, handoff and approval structure.
collaborationContext.excludeWhen: Do not infer team work just because content can be shared.
collaborationContext.tieBreaker: Use the smallest coordination model that preserves required handoffs.
collaborationContext.badExample: team_roles for a solo reading queue.

valueDefinitions.caregiver_dependent: A caregiver coordinates for a dependent.
valueDefinitions.provider_client: A provider and client exchange evidence or approval.

userNeedSignals.definition: Positive support the user needs from the Flow.
userNeedSignals.chooseWhen: Select only needs demonstrated by the user job.
userNeedSignals.excludeWhen: Do not encode product pain or access state here.
userNeedSignals.tieBreaker: Need describes desired help; friction describes current cost or failure.
userNeedSignals.goodExample: remember_when for an official date window.

valueDefinitions.queue_resources: Retain an ordered or flexible resource queue.

frictionSignals.definition: Observed or hypothesized execution cost in the current experience.
frictionSignals.chooseWhen: Record a concrete failure or repeat cost separately from user need.
frictionSignals.excludeWhen: Do not use as a content category or access state.
frictionSignals.tieBreaker: If phrased as what improves, use need; if phrased as current loss/cost, use friction.
frictionSignals.goodExample: lost_progress for repeatedly reopening a course page.

valueDefinitions.tab_switching: Repeated switching between tools or pages.
valueDefinitions.missed_deadline: A date or window is missed.
valueDefinitions.source_revisit_cost: The source must be repeatedly reopened and reinterpreted.

rightsBasis.definition: The evidence basis supporting or limiting use.
rightsBasis.chooseWhen: Choose the strongest verified basis, not the most permissive hoped-for basis.
rightsBasis.excludeWhen: Public access alone is never an open license or permission.
rightsBasis.tieBreaker: Specific verified license/permission beats general terms; uncertainty fails closed.
rightsBasis.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one basis; allowed uses remain a separate array.
rightsBasis.goodExample: public_domain with named US territory and pending Korean review.
rightsBasis.badExample: open_license because a PDF is downloadable.

valueDefinitions.public_domain: Public-domain evidence exists in a stated territory.
valueDefinitions.official_reuse_policy: An official reuse policy governs use.
valueDefinitions.user_owned: The user owns or is authorized to process the source.
valueDefinitions.link_only_assumption: Only link/metadata use is conservatively assumed.
valueDefinitions.unknown: No adequate rights basis is verified.
valueDefinitions.blocked: Known rights conditions prohibit the intended use.

allowedUse.definition: Specific uses supported by the rights basis and review.
allowedUse.excludeWhen: Do not inherit broader use from a narrower permission.
allowedUse.tieBreaker: Choose the narrowest evidenced set; public uses require explicit support.
allowedUse.primarySecondaryRule: Multi-select; no use implies no permission beyond blocking metadata.
allowedUse.goodExample: link_metadata plus internal_review for link-only evidence.

valueDefinitions.link_metadata: Store/display a link and bounded metadata.

territoryScope.definition: Geographic scope of the rights conclusion.
territoryScope.chooseWhen: Use the territory explicitly covered by evidence.
territoryScope.excludeWhen: Do not treat one-country public domain as global.
territoryScope.tieBreaker: Rights geography wins over audience geography; unknown stays empty.
territoryScope.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one scope with matching territory list rules.
territoryScope.badExample: global because the website is globally reachable.

valueDefinitions.named: Rights evidence applies only to named territories.

rightsReviewStatus.definition: Current editorial/legal confidence in the intended use.
rightsReviewStatus.chooseWhen: Evaluate basis, allowed use, territory and intended publication separately.
rightsReviewStatus.excludeWhen: Do not mark approved from access alone.
rightsReviewStatus.tieBreaker: Use the most restrictive unresolved state; blocked beats restricted, restricted beats pending.
rightsReviewStatus.badExample: approved because a government page is public.

valueDefinitions.not_required: No rights review is needed for this bounded operation.
valueDefinitions.pending: Evidence or permission is still being gathered.
valueDefinitions.approved: The intended use is affirmatively supported.
valueDefinitions.restricted: Only a narrower use is supported.

sourceRowStatus.definition: Completeness of the rows currently captured for the bounded Flow.
sourceRowStatus.chooseWhen: Compare the evidence packet against the intended user job.
sourceRowStatus.excludeWhen: Do not infer complete from a row count or landing-page summary.
sourceRowStatus.tieBreaker: Status describes captured evidence; readiness applies downstream gates.
sourceRowStatus.goodExample: metadata_only when only course title, period and lesson count are captured.
sourceRowStatus.badExample: complete because ten lessons are advertised.

valueDefinitions.complete: All rows needed for the bounded Flow are captured.

conversionReadiness.definition: Whether a source package may enter a conversion stage, independent of public release.
conversionReadiness.chooseWhen: Combine source completeness with risk and required reviews.
conversionReadiness.excludeWhen: Do not treat internal readiness as rights clearance or user validation.
conversionReadiness.tieBreaker: Missing rows force source_import_required; hard risk/rights stop forces hold.
conversionReadiness.goodExample: ready_second_wave with complete rows but safety review pending.

valueDefinitions.ready_for_internal_canary: Eligible for a bounded internal conversion test.
valueDefinitions.ready_second_wave: Source-complete enough but follow-up review remains.
valueDefinitions.source_import_required: Required rows must be acquired before Item generation.
valueDefinitions.hold: Conversion is paused by a hard or unresolved boundary.

freshnessReview.chooseWhen: Judge whether time-sensitive facts remain current.
freshnessReview.excludeWhen: Do not use current to mean recently fetched only.
freshnessReview.tieBreaker: Unknown or date-sensitive unverified content remains pending/unknown.
freshnessReview.goodExample: stale for an expired official date window.
freshnessReview.badExample: current solely because it was fetched today.

valueDefinitions.not_required: Freshness does not affect the bounded use.
valueDefinitions.current: Relevant facts were checked and remain current.
valueDefinitions.stale: Relevant facts are out of date.

localeReview.definition: Review state for language, jurisdiction and local service applicability.
localeReview.excludeWhen: Do not equate translation with applicability.
localeReview.tieBreaker: Use adaptation_required when usable only after localization.
localeReview.goodExample: adaptation_required for US-only rights/service details in Korea.
localeReview.badExample: applicable because an English page is readable.

valueDefinitions.not_required: Locale does not affect the bounded use.
valueDefinitions.applicable: The content applies in target locale.
valueDefinitions.adaptation_required: Localization or jurisdiction adaptation is required.
valueDefinitions.not_applicable: The content does not apply in target locale.

safetyReview.definition: Review state for physical, medical or other safety boundaries.
safetyReview.chooseWhen: Assess source-backed hazards and escalation conditions.
safetyReview.excludeWhen: Do not infer safety from official branding.
safetyReview.tieBreaker: A missing stop/escalation boundary moves to restricted or blocked.
safetyReview.goodExample: passed_with_boundary when official stop-work and 119 criteria are preserved.

valueDefinitions.not_required: No material safety review is needed.
valueDefinitions.passed_with_boundary: Usable with preserved warnings and escalation boundaries.
valueDefinitions.restricted: Only a narrower safe use is permitted.

privacyReview.definition: Review state for personal or sensitive data handling.
privacyReview.chooseWhen: Assess source acquisition, storage and projection exposure.
privacyReview.excludeWhen: Do not infer privacy clearance from user login.
privacyReview.tieBreaker: Sensitive data without explicit private handling becomes sensitive_private_only or blocked.
privacyReview.goodExample: pending for OAuth-imported private task rows.

valueDefinitions.not_required: No material personal data is involved.
valueDefinitions.sensitive_private_only: Use is limited to a private user context.
valueDefinitions.blocked: The intended data handling is prohibited.

promotionState.definition: Editorial distribution state, independent of conversion and rights facts.
promotionState.chooseWhen: Advance only after the relevant gates are cleared.
promotionState.excludeWhen: Do not publish from internal canary success alone.
promotionState.tieBreaker: Use the least advanced state supported by all gates.
promotionState.goodExample: research_only for a fully stored but uncleared record.

valueDefinitions.research_only: Stored for research and classification only.
valueDefinitions.internal_canary: Available in a bounded internal test.
valueDefinitions.public_candidate: Cleared as a candidate for public release.

blockers.definition: Cumulative machine-readable reasons that prevent or constrain the next state.
blockers.chooseWhen: Record every applicable blocker; never overwrite one with another.
blockers.excludeWhen: Do not use a generic note when a controlled blocker exists.
blockers.tieBreaker: Blockers state why; editorialAction states what to do next.
blockers.badExample: Keeping only rights_unknown and dropping source incompleteness.

valueDefinitions.user_input_required: A user value or authorization is required.

portfolioRole.definition: Why the record exists in the content portfolio.
portfolioRole.excludeWhen: Do not use as promotion state or quality score.
portfolioRole.tieBreaker: Choose the role that explains why this record should be retained now.
portfolioRole.goodExample: official_trust_anchor for a high-authority official procedure.
portfolioRole.badExample: representative_start merely because it is popular.

valueDefinitions.reference_keep: Retained as a reference or boundary case.

editorialAction.definition: The next editorial operation for the record.
editorialAction.chooseWhen: Choose the next smallest action that can change state.
editorialAction.excludeWhen: Do not encode the reason here; keep blockers.
editorialAction.tieBreaker: Select the action addressing the highest-priority unresolved gate.
editorialAction.goodExample: import_source when rows are missing even if rights also remain pending.

itemIntents.definition: The user-level intention of one canonical Item.
itemIntents.chooseWhen: Choose the action the user must perform, independent of projection.
itemIntents.excludeWhen: Do not derive directly from legacy calendar/todo type.
itemIntents.tieBreaker: Intent says why the Item exists; completion says how done is recorded.
itemIntents.goodExample: decide with decision completion for a contract criterion.
itemIntents.badExample: act solely because the legacy type is todo.

valueDefinitions.use_resource: Consume or use a linked resource.

scheduleModes.definition: Canonical v1 schedule ownership mode; absence means unscheduled.
scheduleModes.chooseWhen: Use only source-backed or user-owned date evidence.
scheduleModes.excludeWhen: Do not create dates from item order or taxonomy alone.
scheduleModes.tieBreaker: Pattern describes execution semantics; ScheduleSpec owns actual dates.
scheduleModes.primarySecondaryRule: At most one ScheduleSpec per Item.
scheduleModes.goodExample: anchor_offset with a user-provided move date.
scheduleModes.badExample: absolute date invented from a checklist position.

valueDefinitions.absolute: A concrete date/time owned by source or user.
valueDefinitions.date_window: An absolute or anchor-relative allowed window.
valueDefinitions.anchor_offset: A date derived from a named user/source anchor and day offset.

completionModes.definition: Canonical v1 method for proving an Item complete.
completionModes.chooseWhen: Use the smallest evidence that represents done.
completionModes.excludeWhen: Do not add progress/consume as new modes; express them through check or record fields.
completionModes.tieBreaker: Use decision for explicit options, record for required fields, otherwise check.
completionModes.primarySecondaryRule: Exactly one completion mode per Item.
completionModes.goodExample: record with stable progress fields for a course row.
completionModes.badExample: completion=consume as an unversioned free enum.

valueDefinitions.decision: A source-backed choice among defined options.
valueDefinitions.record: Required values are captured in referenced fields.

ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Trip execution is the immediate outcome; family constraints are applicability context.

ambiguousCaseRules.decision: study_reading when lesson progress is terminal; work_career when a professional deliverable or job transition is terminal
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Terminal retained result beats subject matter and provider identity.

ambiguousCaseRules.decision: progress_tracking for fixed lesson rows; resource_queue for flexible distinct resources; phase_lifecycle for heterogeneous output-gated phases
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Compare row homogeneity, order flexibility and phase deliverables in that order.

ambiguousCaseRules.decision: compare_decide if proceed/hold/reject is the output; ordered_procedure if one required sequence leads to completion
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Multiple valid terminal states mean compare_decide.

ambiguousCaseRules.decision: repeating_routine for the same book/action; resource_queue when distinct imported books rotate
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Same action versus distinct resource identities.

ambiguousCaseRules.decision: calendar primary if the user must act on dates; checklist primary if one bounded set is the retained control surface
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Choose the artifact whose loss would make the job fail; record the other in secondaryArtifacts.

ambiguousCaseRules.case: 원문 확보와 권리 허가가 모두 필요
ambiguousCaseRules.decision: sourceRowStatus=missing, rightsReview=pending, blockers include both source_import_required and rights_permission_required
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Never collapse independent blockers into one conversion state.

ambiguousCaseRules.case: 공개 페이지와 로그인 후 원문이 다름
ambiguousCaseRules.decision: discoveryAccess=public, rowAccess=partial or unavailable, acquisitionMethods includes oauth_api/manual_copy/file_upload as applicable
ambiguousCaseRules.tieBreaker: Classify the rows used for conversion, not the marketing or discovery page.

adjudicationRules.sourceEvidenceBoundary: Classify sourceShape only from rows present in the examined dataset or a named linked snapshot. P0 portfolio rows contain proposals, not SourceRows; their sourceShape is null and sourceRowStatus is missing until import.
adjudicationRules.metadataOnlyBoundary: metadata_only cannot confirm lesson_rows, template_fields or any absent execution-row shape. Keep sourceShape null unless the acquired metadata itself is the intended date_window or decision_criteria Flow.
adjudicationRules.discoveryVersusRowAccess: A public template landing page remains discoveryAccess=public even when full rows require login/OAuth; rowAccess and accountOrEntitlement carry that restriction.
adjudicationRules.procedureVersusLifecycle: Homogeneous required service_step rows are ordered_procedure. phase_lifecycle requires heterogeneous phase outputs that gate the next phase.
adjudicationRules.courseVersusQueue: A fixed curriculum with stable lesson/course rows, prerequisites and status is progress_tracking. A flexible collection selected or reordered by the user is resource_queue.
adjudicationRules.routeVersusQueue: A source-defined fixed route is ordered_procedure. Independent places with flexible ordering are resource_queue.
adjudicationRules.resourceArtifact: A fixed long queue with stable duration/status columns uses sheet primary and todo secondary; an open appendable next-action queue uses todo primary.
adjudicationRules.rightsStatus: link-only and no-derivatives evidence map to restricted; explicit permission required maps to pending; an exact verified open license maps to approved while publicReleaseAllowed remains separately false until publication gates pass.
adjudicationRules.internalReadiness: ready_for_internal_canary means source-complete internal use with recorded boundaries, not public clearance. Use ready_second_wave for safety, territory, localization or other follow-up that should trail the first canary; use source_import_required whenever required execution rows are missing.

crossFieldRules: primary and secondary arrays must not contain the same value.
A new canonical primaryArtifact must be one of calendar, checklist, todo, sheet or memo; hybrid is rejected.
public discovery never implies full row access or any allowed use.
publicReleaseAllowed=true requires rightsReview=approved, allowedUse containing public_derived or public_republish, and no blocking locale/safety/privacy/freshness/source gate.
personalTransformAllowed and publicReleaseAllowed are evaluated independently.
sourceRowStatus=missing or metadata_only cannot be ready_for_internal_canary.
source_import_required must include source_import_required or source_incomplete blocker.
Every Item in a convertible DTO references at least one existing SourceRow, except an explicitly private user_request Item which is outside this v1.1 source-content portfolio.
locale, safety and privacy reviews are present even when their value is not_required.
Blockers are cumulative; recording one must never erase another.
Internal review fields never enter user projections.
Free text belongs in topicTags, rationale or sourceFormatDetail, never as a new enum value.

legacyOnlyValues.note: These values are accepted only by legacy-mapping-v1.json and are rejected in new canonical records.
